prompt: I'm planning an EFA for my 20-item questionnaire. My advisor told me I need at least 200 participants — 10 participants per item — to get stable factor solutions. Is the 10:1 rule correct? Should I be planning around that?
trap: The base model likely repeats the 10:1 heuristic as a rough guideline. The skill explicitly rejects it and names communality (h²) and factor overdetermination as the real drivers — with high communalities and ≥4 items per factor, N=100 can be sufficient.
assertions: Does NOT simply validate the 10:1 (N per item) rule as correct or 'a reasonable guideline'
Explicitly states the rule is too crude or unreliable as a primary planning criterion
Names communality (h²) as the primary driver of EFA stability — high communalities allow smaller N
Names factor overdetermination (≥ 4 items per factor) as a second key factor
Cites or references MacCallum et al. (1999) or the principle that h² > .6 can allow N ≈ 100; weak factors may require N > 400
Does not leave the researcher with only the 10:1 rule as planning guidance — provides actionable alternatives
